learningObjective: Estimate the throughput impact of warp divergence and identify when divergence does not degrade throughput.
stem: A CUDA kernel executes an if/else branch that produces two disjoint code paths of similar cost (T_A ≈ T_B ≈ T). Which of the following statements about divergence within a warp are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Post-Volta independent thread scheduling changes the SIMT semantics so that both branches now truly execute in parallel within a warp with no serialization cost, eliminating warp divergence entirely.
If all 32 threads in a warp take the same side of the branch, no divergence penalty is incurred; the branch behaves like a single-path warp.
If the warp splits (some threads take path A, others path B), the two subsets execute serially and total warp time is approximately T_A + T_B (both paths are covered under mask), not max(T_A, T_B).
Divergence is per-block, not per-warp; as long as the block executes both branches somewhere, the compiler predicates the whole block uniformly.

explanation: A: SIMT divergence is only an issue when threads in the same warp take different branch sides; a uniform branch has no divergence cost. B: Under divergence, the hardware masks off threads not taking a side and executes each side in turn, so warp wall time ≈ sum of side durations under mask; only threads on each side make progress at a time. C is wrong: divergence is a warp-level property, not block-level. D is wrong: independent thread scheduling improves correctness (deadlock-freedom, reconvergence flexibility) but does not eliminate serialization of divergent paths within a warp.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: Volta+ independent thread scheduling changed reconvergence semantics but did not remove per-warp serialization of divergent branches.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: uniform warps skip the divergence penalty entirely.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: divergent warps serialize the taken/not-taken sides using lane masking.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: divergence is per-warp; different warps in the same block can independently take different sides without penalizing each other.

assumptions: Both branch paths have similar cost T_A ≈ T_B and neither is trivially compiled to predicated math.
Compiler does not automatically predicate the branch away (i.e., real control divergence occurs).
nonImplications: Does not imply that eliminating all branches always helps; small predicated branches may be cheaper than restructuring.
Does not imply divergent warps waste all their bandwidth; masked-off threads still occupy warp slots but do not perform useful work during their masked-off cycles.

distractorRationales.A: Version-leak misinterpretation of independent thread scheduling.

sourceRefs.locator: SIMT architecture, branch divergence, independent thread scheduling
